config.title: Compression & caching

intro.title: Compression & caching
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Express server that uses compression and caching to improve performance. You will learn how to reduce the size of responses sent to clients using the compression middleware and how to cache static files to speed up repeated requests. The main technologies involved are the Express framework, the compression middleware, and the built-in static middleware with cache headers. By the end, you'll understand how these techniques optimize web applications for faster loading and better user experience.
intro.usecase: Compression and caching are essential for optimizing web application performance, especially in data-heavy products like e-commerce platforms and content management systems. For example, an e-commerce dashboard displaying real-time sales analytics benefits from caching API responses to avoid redundant database queries, while compressing product images and JSON payloads reduces page load times. Similarly, a news website with high traffic uses caching for frequently accessed articles and compression for text content to serve users faster. These techniques are crucial for improving user experience, reducing server load, and lowering bandwidth costs in production environments.

objectives: Configure Express middleware to compress HTTP responses
Implement caching headers for static assets in Express routes
Integrate a compression library to reduce response payload size
Construct middleware that applies caching policies to dynamic content
Apply conditional compression based on request headers
Manipulate cache-control directives for different resource types
Initialize a caching strategy for API endpoints to improve performance

steps.title: Import Express and compression middleware
steps.instruction: Import Express and the compression middleware package at the top of your file.
steps.hint: Use the 'require' statement to import both Express and the compression package. The compression middleware is a separate package you'll need to require.
steps.seedCode: // Import Express and compression middleware here
steps.expectedOutcome: The Express framework and compression middleware are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: Both Express and the compression middleware package are imported using require statements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported one of the required modules, but you need both Express and the compression middleware. Make sure to import the 'compression' package as well.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import both Express and the compression middleware using require statements.

steps.title: Create Express app instance
steps.instruction: Create an Express app instance by calling express() and assign it to a constant named 'app'.
steps.hint: Use the imported express function to create your application instance.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating an Express app instance
const app = express();
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have an Express application instance ready to configure with middleware.
successCriteria: An Express app instance is created and assigned to a constant named 'app'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling express() and assigning it to 'app'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to create the app instance using express().

steps.title: Apply compression middleware
steps.instruction: Use app.use() to apply the compression middleware to your Express app.
steps.hint: Call app.use() with the compression middleware function as the argument.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: applying middleware in Express
app.use(express.json());
steps.expectedOutcome: The compression middleware is applied to all incoming requests.
successCriteria: app.use() is called with compression() as its argument.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling app.use() with compression() as the argument.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to apply the compression middleware using app.use().

steps.title: Import caching middleware
steps.instruction: Import the caching middleware package using require() and assign it to a constant named 'cacheMiddleware'.
steps.hint: Use require() to import the package, similar to how you imported express and compression. The package name is 'cache-middleware'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing a middleware package
const session = require('express-session');
steps.expectedOutcome: The caching middleware package is imported and ready to be used in the Express app.
successCriteria: The 'cache-middleware' package is imported and assigned to a constant named 'cacheMiddleware'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing 'cache-middleware' and assigning it to a constant named 'cacheMiddleware'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import the caching middleware package using require().

steps.title: Configure caching middleware
steps.instruction: Configure the caching middleware by setting its duration to 1 hour (3600000 milliseconds).
steps.hint: Use the middleware function with an options object containing a maxAge property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The caching middleware is configured to cache responses for 1 hour.
successCriteria: Caching middleware is configured with maxAge set to 3600000.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've set the maxAge property to 3600000 milliseconds.
steps.feedbackWrong: The caching middleware configuration is missing or incorrect. Check that you've set the maxAge property to 3600000.

steps.title: Apply caching middleware to routes
steps.instruction: Use app.use() to apply the caching middleware to your Express application.
steps.hint: The app.use() method adds middleware to your Express app. Call it with the caching middleware function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The caching middleware will be applied to all routes in your Express application.
successCriteria: app.use() is called with the caching middleware function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using app.use() with the caching middleware function.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to use app.use() to apply the caching middleware to your Express application.

steps.title: Create a test route
steps.instruction: Create a GET route at '/test' that returns a JSON object with a message property set to 'Hello, compressed and cached world!'
steps.hint: Use app.get() with the route path and a callback function that sends a JSON response.
steps.expectedOutcome: A GET route '/test' is added that returns JSON data, which will be compressed and cached when middleware is applied.
successCriteria: The code includes app.get('/test', ...) with a callback that sends a JSON response containing a message property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the route uses '/test' and returns JSON with a message property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test route is missing or incorrect. Ensure you create a GET route at '/test' that returns JSON.

steps.title: Add response headers for caching
steps.instruction: In the test route you created, add a cache-control header to the response using res.setHeader(). Set the header to 'Cache-Control' with a value of 'public, max-age=3600' (one hour).
steps.hint: Use res.setHeader('Cache-Control', 'public, max-age=3600') inside your route handler before sending the response.
steps.expectedOutcome: The route response will include a Cache-Control header that tells browsers and proxies to cache the response for one hour.
successCriteria: The route handler includes res.setHeader('Cache-Control', 'public, max-age=3600') before sending the response.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using res.setHeader() with the correct header name and value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The cache-control header wasn't properly set. Remember to use res.setHeader('Cache-Control', 'public, max-age=3600') in your route handler.

steps.title: Start the server
steps.instruction: Start the Express server by calling app.listen() on port 3000.
steps.hint: Use app.listen(3000, callback) to start the server and log a message when it's running.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will be configured to listen on port 3000 with a confirmation log message.
successCriteria: app.listen() is called with port 3000 and a callback function that logs a message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling app.listen() with both the port number and a callback function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server isn't properly started. Check that you're using app.listen(3000, callback) with a console.log message.

steps.title: Test the compression and caching
steps.instruction: Start your Express server and test the compression and caching by making a request to the test route using a browser or tool like curl.
steps.hint: Run your server file with Node.js, then open a browser to http://localhost:3000/test or use curl -I http://localhost:3000/test to see response headers.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server starts successfully, and requests to the test route show compression headers (like Content-Encoding: gzip) and caching headers (like Cache-Control).
successCriteria: Server starts without errors, and test route responses include compression and caching headers.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: The server started, but make sure to check the response headers for both compression (Content-Encoding) and caching (Cache-Control) to confirm they're applied.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server didn't start or the test route isn't responding. Check that all middleware and routes are correctly configured and the server is listening on the correct port.
